hypotheses.claim: ClayCode can permit cyclic structural module/link graphs while retaining deterministic startup if linking is separated from eager value initialization and only the eager value-dependency graph is required to be acyclic.
hypotheses.prediction: Programs with import/link SCCs but acyclic eager value dependencies compile/link and produce identical semantic results under module discovery/import-order perturbation.
hypotheses.falsifier: A production ClayCode case where structural cyclic linking necessarily induces order-sensitive eager state, or a valid program whose semantics differ under the proposed split.

hypotheses.claim: Eager initialization cycles should fail closed with a canonical SCC-based cycle receipt rather than exposing partially initialized default state.
hypotheses.prediction: The same eager dependency cycle yields the same normalized cycle membership/internal-edge receipt and hash despite parser/import/discovery ordering.
hypotheses.falsifier: Canonical cycle receipts cannot be made stable without discarding semantically relevant dependency distinctions, or production semantics require a valid eager recursive initialization case.

hypotheses.claim: No new ClayCode surface syntax is needed for BASE module-cycle semantics; canonical IR/linker/runtime metadata can express the distinction between structural references and eager initialization dependencies.
hypotheses.prediction: A production implementation can realize the module/link/init plan using existing module/import/value/function/type constructs plus compiler metadata.
hypotheses.falsifier: An executable application or FRANK component requires explicit user-visible lazy/phase/init semantics that cannot be represented or inferred safely.

counterhypotheses.claim: Ban all direct and indirect module import cycles.
counterhypotheses.reason: Simpler but rejects generated structural-cycle cases whose eager value-dependency graph is acyclic and deterministic.

counterhypotheses.claim: Allow recursive initialization by exposing partial/default module state.
counterhypotheses.reason: Naive partial initialization generated order-sensitive final results and uninitialized reads; production JVM-style guarded semantics remain a comparison, not refuted in full.

counterhypotheses.claim: Use one fixed source/import traversal order and treat that as sufficient determinism.
counterhypotheses.reason: A fixed traversal can hide semantic dependence on arbitrary presentation order; the proposed contract instead derives readiness from semantic eager dependencies.

counterhypotheses.claim: Adopt full live-binding/TDZ cyclic evaluation semantics immediately.
counterhypotheses.reason: ECMAScript demonstrates that cyclic module SCCs are implementable, but ClayCode has no executable counterexample yet requiring the additional runtime complexity.

counterhypotheses.claim: Add explicit lazy initialization syntax now.
counterhypotheses.reason: Violates the current less-change-more-compile policy absent a concrete application/compiler counterexample.

proposed_minimal_contract.phase_1_link: Resolve all module semantic identities and structural type/function/symbol bindings across SCCs without executing eager values.
proposed_minimal_contract.phase_2_init_graph: Derive eager initialization dependency edges from canonical typed IR, not textual import order.
proposed_minimal_contract.phase_3_execute: Initialize ready eager values in deterministic order keyed by stable semantic identity when multiple nodes are simultaneously ready.
proposed_minimal_contract.phase_4_cycle: If eager nodes remain in SCCs, fail closed before exposing module-ready state and emit a canonical ModuleInitCycleReceipt.
